title: Reliable Semantic Communication With QoE-Driven Resource Scheduling for UAV-Assisted MEC
abstract: Semantic communication is a great potential technology to improve the reliability and effectiveness of communication systems, but the limited computing capacity of users, the potential jamming attacks, and the inflexibility of fixed base stations pose significant challenges to communication efficiency. To overcome those challenges, this paper proposes a joint resource scheduling approach for unpiloted aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted mobile edge computing (MEC) system based on reliable semantic communications against malicious jamming attacks. Specifically, we maximize the system's quality-of-experience (QoE) by jointly optimizing UAV trajectory, task offloading decision, and user association. Since the problem is non-convex and the jamming behavior is dynamic, an advanced softmax deep double deterministic policy gradients (SD3) based on the prioritized experience replay (PER) algorithm (called PER-SD3) is designed to realize an efficient communication strategy against jamming. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed PER-SD3 approach can significantly improve the system delay and semantic communication performances compared with baseline approaches in the literature.

title: SNR Adaptive Attention Joint Source Channel Coding for Enhanced Image Transmission in Wireless Vehicular System
abstract: Reliable image transmission is critical for applications such as autonomous driving, collision avoidance, and real time traffic monitoring in the field of vehicles. However, extreme and dynamic vehicular environments impose significant challenges on reliable image transmission. Traditional communication methods that separately design source and channel coding fail to fully exploit the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) information in vehicular channels and lead to suboptimal performance. Although recent deep learning (DL) based approaches have shown promising results in enhancing image transmission, they are often constrained by high storage requirements and limited adaptability to the highly variable channel conditions in vehicular environments. In this paper, a novel DL-based SNR adaptive attention joint source channel coding (SAA-JSCC) framework tailored for vehicular wireless communication systems is proposed. The proposed SAA-JSCC dynamically adjusts encoding and decoding strategies in real time by leveraging instantaneous SNR feedback, thereby optimizing transmission efficiency and reliability. A deep neural network is employed to directly map input RGB images to complex-valued baseband samples, while the receiver integrates the decoding and decision-making processes within its neural architecture. Comprehensive simulations under diverse vehicular channel conditions demonstrate that the SAA-JSCC approach significantly outperforms existing JSCC methods in terms of Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) for image transmission, particularly under low SNR scenarios prevalent in vehicular environments. Furthermore, the proposed method delivers significant PSNR gain with a modest increase in FLOPs and negligible parameter growth, while remaining far smaller model size than prior deep baselines, thereby facilitating more efficient and scalable real time communication in next-generation vehicular networks.

title: CSI Feedback via Joint Source-Channel Coding and Modulation: A Comprehensive Study for 6G Realization
abstract: In modern wireless systems, the process of acquiring channel state information (CSI) has become increasingly critical yet challenging, driven by the conflicting needs of expanding antenna arrays and the pursuit of high spectral efficiency. Recent research particularly leveraging joint source-channel coding and modulation (JSCM) via autoencoder architectures, has demonstrated initial promise in significantly enhancing CSI feedback effectiveness. However, a substantial gap persists between algorithm research and practical realization, particularly concerning real-world validation and systematic design methodologies. This article introduces a comprehensive framework enabling JSCM-based CSI feedback, which encompasses a learning methodology robust against wireless channel imperfection and protocol designs tailored for seamless integration into practical cellular systems. A hardware proof-of-concept (PoC) platform is developed and deployed, where experimental results substantiate the proposed method's superiority in realistic wireless environments. Furthermore, by synergizing technical and protocol innovations, this article resolves three critical challenges impeding the deployment of JSCM-based CSI feedback in future 6G networks: variant resource allocation, low peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) waveforms design, and accurate channel quality indication (CQI) estimation. Equipped with these enabling techniques, the proposed JSCM-based CSI feedback solution is positioned for 6G adoption, demonstrating substantial throughput improvements over conventional separate source and channel coding (SSCC) implementations.

title: Design of a Speech Enhancement-Based Deep Semantic Autoencoder for Wireless Communications
abstract: Speech communication plays a crucial role in the Internet of Things and autonomous networks. However, traditional communication systems suffer from insufficient semantic extraction and limited noise suppression capability. To address these issues, we propose a Speech enhancement-based Deep Semantic Autoencoder (S-DSA) for wireless communications. It consists of a dual-branch semantic encoder, a channel encoder, a channel decoder, and two semantic decoders, enabling joint source-channel coding for robust transmission. A key novelty lies in an adaptive semantic noise decoupling mechanism that disentangles target speech semantics from noise representations through an interaction module, thus maintaining semantic consistency under low SNR conditions. Furthermore, a joint training strategy optimizes speech reconstruction and noise estimation, while a lightweight testing strategy reduces complexity by disabling the noise-decoding path. the proposed S-DSA enables more effective separation between speech and noise, and yields higher robustness as well as better reconstruction quality. These findings highlight the potential of the proposed S-DSA as a practical solution for next-generation intelligent communication systems.

title: Goal-Oriented Semantic Communication for Multi-Robots Odor Source Localization
abstract: In robotic odor source localization (OSL), the chemical plume is released by an odor source and dispersed by airflow. The cooperation of multi-robots can shorten the time to find and track the plume, so as to reduce the time to locate the odor source. Current research works on multi-robots OSL mainly focus on the control process, while the communication process is neglected. Although traditional bit-oriented communication framework can shed light on this issue, it may cause redundant information transmission and a waste of wireless resources. To this end, this paper designs a goal-oriented semantic communication framework (GSCF) for multi-robots OSL. Specifically, for the plume finding stage, we propose an age of information (AoI) based queue ranking mechanism to prioritize fresh uplink sensor data. For the plume tracking stage, we propose effectiveness-aware uplink sensor data retrieval, value of information (VoI) based queue ranking and AoI based sensor data discard mechanisms to guarantee the successful transmission of high-concentration sensor data. We further propose a maximum concentration gradient based gradient fusion (MCG-GF) algorithm to jointly utilize the effectiveness level information of multiple robots. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed GSCF can reduce the OSL time by at least 11.12% when compared to the traditional bit-oriented multi-robots OSL approach, which verifies that prioritizing semantically critical sensor data can substantially improve localization efficiency.

title: Joint Trajectory-Resource Optimization for UAV Semantic Communication Systems
abstract: Nowadays, semantic communication (SC) has attracted intensive attention. By adopting an “Understand-before-transmit” approach supported by Deep Learning (DL), SC is capable of only sending semantic information (SI) rather than raw data, thereby conserving data transmission and communication costs without any degradation in performance. This makes SC particularly suitable for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) communications, given that UAVs' limitations in size, weight, and power (SWaP). The SWaP constraint limits UAVs' airborne data collection capabilities, and affects the efficiency of large file transmissions, such as images and videos. This work explores the application of SC in UAV communications and proposes a UAV Semantic Communication (UAV-SC) system designed to expedite the wireless image transmission tasks of UAVs. Utilizing a Joint Source-Channel Coding (JSCC) method, we achieve image transmission based on SC between the UAV and the ground vehicles (GV). Subsequently, we develop a joint optimization algorithm for UAV trajectory and resource allocation to identify the near-optimal network configuration for UAV-SC, thereby enhancing overall communication performance. According to the numerical results from simulation, the joint algorithm supports the UAV-SC system working in an energy-efficient way and outperforms benchmark solutions.

title: SAGEComm: Semantic-Aware Generation and Encoding for Next-Gen Communication
abstract: Vehicular technology encompasses the electronic systems, communication protocols, and control mechanisms that enable modern transportation systems. In this context, we propose SAGEComm-Semantic-Aware Generation and Encoding for Communication-a next-generation semantic communication framework that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and channel-aware vector compression. To overcome limitations of prior approaches, including inflexible compression, static retrieval, and the inability to control semantic-cost trade-offs, SAGEComm adopts a principled, modular design. A hybrid optimization algorithm jointly adjusts the semantic quantizer, channel-aware retrieval module, and generative decoder, enabling robust adaptation to dynamic channel conditions (e.g., signal-to-noise ratio, delay, fading) while preserving semantic fidelity. Furthermore, a Semantic Transmission Cost (STC) metric is introduced to evaluate the tradeoffs among semantic fidelity, compression efficiency, and total processing latency. Simulation results indicate that SAGEComm consistently surpasses existing semantic communication systems in semantic fidelity, compression performance, and end-to-end latency. This work underscores the critical role of integrating deep language understanding with physical-layer adaptation to achieve reliable, efficient, and intelligent communications for 6G vehicular networks and beyond.

title: ZeroSC-SR: Importance-Aware Zero-Shot Semantic Speech Communication Over Fading Channels
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative Zero-Shot Semantic Communication System with Speech Reconstruction (ZeroSC-SR), designed to enhance speech transmission and reconstruction in frequency-selective fading channels while remaining compatible with standard digital coding and modulation. By efficiently transmitting phoneme sequences and compressed prompt acoustic features as discrete indices, ZeroSC-SR reduces transmitted data size and achieves a high compression ratio, resulting in lower Character Error Rate (CER) and higher speaker similarity at low transmit power under noisy channels. We quantitatively evaluate the semantic importance of the transmitted phoneme sequences and acoustic features through a task-oriented, mutual-information-based approach. These insights directly guide the development of our Iterative Importance-Aware Allocation and Power Scheduling (IIAPS) strategy, which enhances transmission quality in frequency selective fading channels by allocating subcarriers and power based on semantic importance. Experimental results show that, under fixed power with SNR sweeps, IIAPS outperforms baseline allocation strategies on Word Error Rate (WER) and speaker similarity. Compared to conventional systems, ZeroSC-SR de livers lower CER and higher speaker similarity under varying transmit power, with the greatest improvements occurring at lower power levels.
